lede: Quraysh had tried threats and tried mockery, and now they tried a bargain: worship our gods for a year, and we will worship yours for a year. The reply closed that door for good.

names.name: al-Kāfirūn
names.note: After those it addresses. In the hadith it goes by its opening words, Qul yā ayyuhā l-kāfirūn.

names.name: Sūratā al-Ikhlāṣ
names.note: A name given to this surah and al-Ikhlāṣ together, because the Prophet ﷺ recited them as a pair: this one clears worship of every partner, that one clears belief.

revelation.detail: That it is Makkan is the saying of Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan and the majority; that it is Madinan is reported from Qatādah, and al-Qurṭubī adds one of two reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Its occasion settles it for most: the people it answers are the leaders of Quraysh, and the offer they made belongs to the years when they still hoped he could be bought off.
revelation.when: The early years in Makkah, when Quraysh still hoped to strike a bargain

evidence.quote: وَفِيها قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، والحَسَنُ، والجُمْهُورُ. والثّانِي: مَدَنِيَّةٌ، رُوِيَ عَنْ قَتادَةَ
وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَالْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ. وَمَدَنِيَّةٌ فِي أَحَدِ قَوْلَيِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وقتادة والضحاك. وهي ست آيات

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ﴿قُلْ يا أيُّها الكافِرُونَ﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

attested.quote: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، والحَسَنِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ
attested.says: Makkan, in the saying of Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrimah.

setting: The idolaters of Makkah did not ask Muḥammad ﷺ to stop believing in Allah. They believed in Allah themselves. What they could not accept was that He be worshipped alone, with their gods left out — and so the compromises they offered were always about that.

The reports name the men: al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, Umayyah ibn Khalaf.{reported} In one account they went through his uncle al-ʿAbbās; in another they came to him themselves. Come, they said: you worship what we worship for a year, and we will worship what you worship for a year. If what you have is better, we will have had our share of it; and if what we have is better, you will have had yours.

By the standards of the time it was a generous offer, and a man seeking position would have taken it. The surah has him refuse it in four different ways — for now and for the future, in what he worships and in how — and then draws the line: to you your religion, and to me mine. It is not a statement that the two are equally valid. It is a declaration that they will never be mixed.

occasions.title: A year for a year
occasions.text: In their ignorance they invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to worship their idols for a year, and they would worship the One he worshipped for a year. So Allah sent down this surah, commanding His Messenger to declare himself free of their religion altogether.
occasions.source: Ibn Kathīr, on the surah. Al-Ṭabarī, al-Baghawī, al-Qurṭubī, al-Suyūṭī and al-Shawkānī relate it too, and Ibn al-Jawzī gives it as one of three accounts of who made the offer.

evidence.quote: دَعَوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِلَى عِبَادَةِ أَوْثَانِهِمْ سَنَةً، وَيَعْبُدُونَ مَعْبُودَهُ سَنَةً، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ السُّورَةَ، وَأَمَرَ رَسُولَهَ ﷺ فِيهَا أَنْ يَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْ دِينِهِمْ بِالْكُلِّيَّةِ

aim: To establish that worship is for Allah alone, to declare freedom from shirk, and to mark the complete separation of Islam from it.

outline.title: Say
outline.summary: Say: O disbelievers — I do not worship what you worship.

outline.title: Neither now nor ever
outline.summary: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor will I be a worshipper of what you have worshipped; nor will you be worshippers of what I worship. The repetition is the refusal: present and future, the object of worship and the manner of it.

outline.title: The line
outline.summary: To you your religion, and to me my religion.

keyAyah.why: The sentence the offer was answered with. It is a parting of ways, not a truce.

virtues.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited, in the two units before the dawn prayer, “Qul yā ayyuhā l-kāfirūn” and “Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad”.
In his Pilgrimage he ﷺ recited the same two surahs in the two units of prayer after going round the House.
The Prophet ﷺ said to Nawfal: “Recite ‘Qul yā ayyuhā l-kāfirūn’, then sleep upon its ending, for it is a declaration of freedom from shirk.”
virtues.narrator: Farwah ibn Nawfal, from his father

before: Al-Kawthar commanded: pray to your Lord, and sacrifice. Al-Kāfirūn has him tell those who do both for other than Allah that he will have no part in it.
after: The disbelievers were told: to you your religion. Al-Naṣr shows how the matter ended — the help of Allah, the opening of Makkah, and those same tribes entering His religion in crowds.

notable.label: I do not worship what you worship
To you your religion, and to me mine

sources: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī
